title: Knowledge base
text:
1.1 Research areas within scientific fields
Scientific fields (SFs) can be further divided into research areas (RAs). For example, the scientific field of Mathematics can be divided into the following research areas:

Mathematics > Pure Mathematics
Mathematics > Applied Mathematics
Mathematics > Computational Mathematics

title: Knowledge base
section: 1.2 The table of contents of the knowledge base
text:
1.2 The table of contents of the knowledge base
The table of contents of the knowledge base is automatically generated based on the structure of the knowledge base. It is organized by scientific field and research area.

1.2.1 A research area is loosely defined
It should be noted that a research area is loosely defined and can be further divided into sub-areas. For example, the research area of Mathematics > Pure Mathematics can be further divided into the following sub-areas:

Mathematics > Pure Mathematics > Algebra
Mathematics > Pure Mathematics > Analysis
Mathematics > Pure Mathematics > Geometry



1.2.2 The research areas can span theoretical and applied research
For example, the research area of Mathematics > Applied Mathematics can include both theoretical and applied aspects of mathematics.

title: Knowledge base
text:
2.1 Text and equations
Textual content and mathematical equations are certainly the most frequent type of content.

2.1.1 Textual content
For example, you can write a paragraph of text like this:
`` The riemann hypothesis was initially proposed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859. It is a conjecture about the distribution of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, which is a complex function that encodes information about the prime numbers. The hypothesis states that all non-trivial zeros of the zeta function have a real part equal to 1/2. This conjecture has profound implications for number theory and has been the subject of extensive research and study. ”
